title: Light During Root Initiation
objective: Balance photosynthetic support, heat load, and water demand during root initiation.
coreScience: Light supplies energy for photosynthesis and signals development, but an unrooted cutting has restricted hydraulic capacity. Excess photon load or radiant heat can raise leaf temperature and water demand faster than the cutting can replace water.

Very low light can preserve water while limiting carbohydrate supply and delaying functional growth. The useful range depends on donor reserves, leaf area, temperature, humidity, spectrum, genotype, and progression of rooting.

Cannabis propagation studies use different fixtures and conditions, and donor-light treatments can change mother architecture and cutting performance. A fixture label does not define the cutting’s actual exposure.
cultivationRelevance: Map PPFD across the tray and record photoperiod, DLI, spectrum, fixture distance, leaf temperature, and rooting stage. Increase light only after roots and water regulation are demonstrated.

measureAndRecord.requirement: PPFD map; DLI; photoperiod; fixture and spectrum; leaf temperature; tray position; rooting time; wilt, bleaching, elongation, and transplant performance.

misconceptions: More light always creates faster roots.
A propagation lamp setting transfers unchanged between shelves.
evidenceLimits: Cannabis-specific optimum-light evidence is limited and protocol-dependent. Do not publish one universal PPFD target.
